chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father (peace be upon him),

that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) raced the cavalry horses that were prepared, from Al-Hafya to the mosque of the Banu Zureiq, and awarded them from three palm trees (clusters of dates). So he gave the first one a cluster, and gave the second one a cluster, and gave the third one a cluster.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him),

key_terms.مَسْجِدِ بَنِي زُرَيْقٍ: The mosque of the Banu Zureiq clan

ai.seo_question: What was the prize for the horse race organized by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in Al-Kafi, highlights the Prophet’s (peace be upon him and his family) encouragement of physical fitness and martial readiness through horse racing, a practice deeply valued in Shia tradition as part of preparing for jihad. The uniform reward of date clusters (‘udh) to the winner, the participant, and the third place underscores the Islamic principle of incentivizing participation and effort, not just victory. Scholars note this as evidence for the permissibility of prizes in sports competitions, reinforcing the importance of maintaining strength and skill among the Muslim community.
